title: A spec is written end to end with the MCP tools, as the plugin starts them
when: Starts `lathe mcp` on a new product repo as the plugin does, writes a domain, aggregate, entity with its fields, command, event, capability, use case, requirement, interface, flow, step and test through each aggregate's own tools, then tries a step that invokes an event.
then: Expects every call to succeed, `command_next_id` for a command under `TL-LEND-EN01` to give `TL-LEND-CMD01`, the step invoking an event refused as an error, and the data files and the loaded spec as the tools wrote them.

title: The MCP server answers initialize, tools/list and tools/call over stdio
when: Serves MCP over a stream on a fixture product and sends `initialize`, `tools/list`, `view_add_view`, `product_declare_product_kind`, `tools/list` again, an unknown method and a line that is not JSON.
then: Expects `initialize` answered with protocol `2025-06-18`, tools that announce `listChanged` and the server `lathe`; `tools/list` to include `view_add_view`; the view added and written to `data/view.jsonl`; the product kind declared, one `notifications/tools/list_changed` sent and the second list offering `extension_record_add_extension_record`; `Method not found: nope` (-32601) for the unknown method and `Parse error` (-32700) for the line that is not JSON.

title: The MCP launcher starts the repo's own lathe mcp for the project folder
when: Runs the plugin's `scripts/mcp-server.mjs` with `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` set to a product repo, sending `initialize` and a `product_get_product` call; then with it set to an empty folder.
then: Expects the repo's own lathe mcp to answer, and a reason when the folder is no Lathe repo.

title: The MCP tools are the check and one per aggregate command and query, with no generic verb
when: Lists the tools for a product with a record of every kind.
then: Expects the check, then one tool per command and query, named <aggregate>_<command>, none of add, set, move, link, unlink, remove, show, list or next_id, and each input schema typed from its fields' columns.

title: The check tool reports errors, warnings and each product's coverage as lathe check --json gives it
when: Calls the check tool on a product with gaps.
then: Expects the counts, the problems and each product's coverage with its gaps, and an error result exactly when there is an error.

title: An unknown tool is refused and changes nothing
when: Calls a tool the server does not have.
then: Expects a refusal naming the tool.

title: Merges two branches that each added a row, through git with the driver set up as the README says
when: In a new git repo with the `lathe-data` merge driver set up and `.gitattributes` naming `data/*.jsonl`, two branches each add a different row to `data/view.jsonl`, and one is merged into the other.
then: Expects the merge to finish with the file holding both added rows beside the base rows, in order.

title: History runs git itself, inside the product root
when: Runs `git rev-parse --show-prefix` through `runGit` in the product repo.
then: Expects git, run through runGit against a real temporary repo, to run at the product root.

title: git runs with an argument array, which no shell reads, and changes nothing
when: Runs git through runGit with shell text in an argument, against a real temporary repo.
then: Expects the shell text to stay text (no file made) and the repo's status unchanged.

title: git output is cut at the output cap and stopped at the time limit
when: Runs git log -p through runGit with a 64-character cap, then with a zero time limit.
then: Expects the output cut at the cap and marked, and the run stopped and marked as timed out.

title: The merge fails when one ID is added on both sides with different content
when: Merges a view file whose ours and theirs each add `TL-V02`, one titled `Desk` and the other `Return desk`.
then: Expects the clash `TL-V02 was added on both sides with different content`, and the merged text holding both versions between `<<<<<<< ours`, `=======` and `>>>>>>> theirs`.

title: On this Mac, recorded speech is recognized on-device and read by the chat's grammar
when: On macOS 26 or later, with the Parakeet model fetched and loaded, runs the speech helper on three recorded fixtures (a wake, a message and "Lathe, send"; "lathe" mid-sentence; a question then a statement) and reads its lines with the app's dictation.
then: Expects one wake and "Zoom into this. Then send it to the team." sent, no wake mid-sentence, and the question's pitch rising and the statement's falling.
notes: Skipped off macOS 26. The first run builds the helper and fetches the model (about 0.6 GB) before the tests are timed.

title: A data file changed on disk is heard through fs.watch, read again and announced
when: With serve running on a product and its change stream open, rewrites a use case's title in its data file directly on disk.
then: Expects a spec:changed event naming the use case table and the record summaries, and the next read to hold the new title.
